plant.description: A small electric heater with a temperature sensor. Input u in [0,1] is heater power; the device loses heat to the room on its own. Output y in [0,1] is a normalized temperature reading (0 = 15 °C, 1 = 75 °C).

objective.notes: Maximize time in band and minimize tracking error; lower actuation energy is better at equal tracking.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Direction/magnitude of gain and lag: a first mid-level hold discriminates heating vs no response and measures rise rate and curvature needed for all later control design.
experiments.expected_observation: If positive-gain heater with lag is correct, y will rise monotonically from ~0.17 toward ~0.3-0.5 over 200 s with initially small slope that grows then flattens; end value clearly above start value and final slope still positive if not fully settled.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Decay behavior at u=0, ambient level, and cooling time constant / lag symmetry, which determines steady-state gain, hold power for 0.5, and controller integral time.
experiments.expected_observation: If self-cooling first-order hypothesis is right, y will decay monotonically from ~0.56 toward ~0.15-0.25 over 480 s with most negative slope early (~-0.001 to -0.003 per s) flattening toward zero, crossing target 0.5 within tens of seconds; final 5-s slope near zero if settled, noise visible as +/-0.01-0.02 with possible larger dips as in E1.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input needed to hold target 0.5 and linearity: second amplitude at 0.4 discriminates whether 0.5 overshoots and estimates gain/intercept for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If linear first-order heater with hold power ~0.42 is right, y will rise monotonically from ~0.16 toward ~0.42-0.50 over 270 s with steepest slope early ~0.001-0.002/s flattening late; end value clearly above start but below E1 equilibrium (~0.55), final 5-s slope small positive if near settling. Overshoot above 0.55 or no rise would falsify gain/linearity estimate.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state input to hold target 0.5 and linearity at a third amplitude: 0.3 discriminates whether y holds near band versus decays well below, fixing feedforward and gain for control.
experiments.expected_observation: If gain ~1.0 with ambient ~0.17 and hold ~0.33 is right, y starting ~0.54 will stay flat or drift slowly down toward ~0.48-0.52 over 150 s with small negative slope flattening toward zero, staying near band; noise +/-0.03 with occasional larger negative dips. Clear decay below 0.45 would imply lower gain/higher hold, rise above 0.58 would imply even 0.3 overshoots.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Steady-state hold power for y=0.5 and linearity at a third amplitude: 0.3 from above discriminates whether equilibrium is near band versus far below, fixing feedforward gain for control.
experiments.expected_observation: Starting ~0.58 above expected equilibrium for u=0.3, y will decay gradually toward ~0.43-0.50 over 140 s with small negative slope early (~-0.001 to -0.002/s) flattening late, staying near/just above band; noise +/-0.03 with occasional larger negative dips as in E1-E3. Flat hold near 0.58 or rise would falsify positive-loss model; fast drop below 0.40 would imply hold power higher than 0.30-0.35.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether u=0.3 equilibrium is at/above/below target 0.5 after settling, which fixes feedforward hold power and gain intercept needed for controller.
experiments.expected_observation: Starting ~0.55 at u=0.3 from above, y will decay only slowly toward ~0.45-0.55 over 160 s with small negative slope flattening late, staying near/just above band; noise +/-0.03 with occasional larger negative dips as in E1-E5. Flat hold near 0.55 would imply equilibrium for 0.3 is at/above 0.55 and hold <0.3; fast drop below 0.45 would imply hold >0.3.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Whether u=0.3 equilibrium is at/above/below target 0.5 after further settling, which fixes feedforward hold power and gain intercept and measures cooling time constant needed for controller integral time.
experiments.expected_observation: Starting ~0.57 above expected equilibrium for u=0.3, y will decay slowly toward ~0.45-0.54 over 150 s with small negative slope early (~-0.001 to -0.002/s) flattening late, staying near/just above band; noise +/-0.03 with occasional larger negative dips to ~0.50 as in E1-E5. Flat hold near 0.56 would imply equilibrium >=0.56 and hold <0.3; fast drop below 0.44 would imply hold well above 0.3.

experiments.uncertainty_targeted: Precise steady-state hold power for y=0.5 and near-target variance, which fixes feedforward and determines whether integral/filtering can keep time-in-band despite large noise.
experiments.expected_observation: Starting ~0.54 above expected equilibrium for u=0.25, y will decay slowly toward ~0.48-0.52 over 180 s with small negative slope early (~-0.001/s) flattening late, staying near/just above band 0.475-0.525; noise +/-0.03 with occasional larger negative dips to ~0.48 as in E1-E3/E5/E7. Flat hold near 0.55 would imply equilibrium >=0.55 and hold <0.25; fast drop below 0.44 would imply hold well above 0.25.

ledger.statement: Heater has positive steady-state gain: higher constant u yields higher equilibrium y.
Step response has appreciable lag: time constant order 150-250 s (~200 s) to approach equilibrium.
No large dead zone: even u=0.3-0.5 produces a clear rise compared to u=0.
At u=0, y decays on its own toward low ambient near 0.12-0.20 due to heat loss.
Steady-state gain is approximately linear in u across 0 to 0.5 with slope ~1.0-1.4 per unit u.
Constant u near 0.5 holds y near target 0.5 at equilibrium.
Sensor noise and short-term fluctuations are small (<~0.01) compared to control band width 0.05.
Steady-state input needed to hold y=0.5 is ~0.24-0.29, below 0.3, because u=0.3 settled near ~0.55 with flat slope while u=0.4 and 0.5 exceeded 0.5 while still rising.
